title: Distribution and volume based scoring for Isolation Forests
summary: The paper generalizes Isolation Forest in two independent places: it replaces the mean-over-trees aggregation with an α-parametrized family hα, and it replaces depth-based per-tree scores with a hypervolume-based score φPAC. It motivates both variants on synthetic data and evaluates IFα and PACα with 100 estimators on 34 ADBench datasets using AUCROC. IFα slightly improves over IF on average for small α, while PACα is worse on average but much better on selected datasets, including annthyroid with AUCROC 91.47 at α=0.5 versus 82.12 for IF/SOTA.

match_target.why: Directly matches the requested metric, dataset, and α=0.5; it is the cheapest single-dataset run that still demonstrates the paper's PACα contribution, requiring one 100-tree forest on annthyroid rather than a 34-dataset sweep.

tolerance.why: Rule 2: no standard deviation is reported for the target value; AUCROC is printed as a percentage on ADBench's annthyroid test split, which has 2,000+ examples under the ADBench protocol, so use a 1.0 absolute AUCROC-point band.

requirements.stmt: Fit standard isolation trees: each node uses a random feature/split, growing until a leaf is pure/singleton or a maximum depth is reached.
requirements.quote: each tree is grown randomly until either a leaf node contains only a single point

requirements.stmt: Use the depth-based per-estimator score φIF = d_i(x)/c_|Y| for the standard IF and IFα baselines.
requirements.quote: where di(x) equals the depth of the leaf node associated to point x

requirements.stmt: Implement the hα aggregation from fα and hα(x)=2^{-fα(x)} for the paper's α grid.
requirements.quote: This leads to the corresponding aggregation functions for α ≥0, hα(x) = 2−fα(x)

requirements.stmt: Ensure α=0 reproduces the standard Isolation Forest aggregation 2^{-mean(φ)}.
requirements.quote: interpolate between the standard IF aggregation function on the one end (α = 0)

requirements.stmt: Implement the PAC per-tree score φPAC = (|L(x)|/|Y|)·(V(Y)/V(L(x))).
requirements.quote: the first of the two factors in the RHS of (1) constitutes a density estimate

requirements.stmt: Define V(L) as the volume of the axis-aligned leaf hyperrectangle and V(Y) as a bounding-volume hyperparameter containing Y.
requirements.quote: V (Y) denotes some bounding volume that contains all points in Y but whose total size is a hyperparameter of the algorithm.

requirements.stmt: Use exactly 100 estimators for every IF/PAC variant.
requirements.quote: For the isolation forest and its variants, we used 100 estimators

requirements.stmt: Sweep α over {0,0.5,1,2,∞} and report the best α per dataset.
requirements.cite: Sec III-A, Setup; Table I caption

requirements.stmt: Evaluate on the 34 ADBench datasets for which AUCROC is not None, using ADBench code for data/benchmark.
requirements.quote: We ran the experiments on 34 datasets, using the code provided in [3]

requirements.stmt: Compute AUCROC from continuous anomaly scores, with higher scores indicating anomalies.
Report best α (and best SOTA algorithm) in parentheses next to each AUCROC in Table I.
requirements.quote: The best value of α and best SOTA algorithm are given in parentheses behind the AUCROC value.

requirements.stmt: Use the authors' custom implementation of the new scoring and aggregation methods, not only ADBench's IF implementation.
requirements.quote: using a custom implementation of the above methods

requirements.stmt: Orient the final aggregated score so that anomalies receive higher scores.
requirements.quote: anomalies correspond to points with higher anomaly score

data.name: ADBench benchmark datasets (annthyroid, cover, landsat, thyroid, Waveform, wine, WPBC, and the other datasets with non-None AUCROC)
data.how_to_get: Use the ADBench code/data release referenced as [3], e.g. https://github.com/Minqi824/ADBench; follow its preprocessing and splits for the 34 datasets with an AUCROC value.

data.name: Generated toy cube dataset for Fig. 2
data.how_to_get: Generate N=128 points in d=10: 127 inliers uniform in the unit cube and one outlier at (1.05,0.5,...,0.5), as described in Sec II-A.

data.name: Generated toy sphere dataset for Fig. 3
data.how_to_get: Generate N=127 points uniformly on a (d-1)-sphere with Gaussian noise plus one outlier at the origin, as described in Sec II-B.
